newsitem.title: USA: Qualcomm says Motorola suit baseless.
newsitem.headline: Qualcomm says Motorola suit baseless.

text.p: Qualcomm Inc said early Friday that the latest in a stringe of patent infringement lawsuits filed against it by Motorola Inc is groundless and an attempt to bully it into renegotiating a contract and royalty arrangement.
Qualcomm, a digital wireless company, said the patents cited in the lawsuit are not specific to any of its "code division multiple access" products.

"Motorola's filings appear to be an attempt to bully Qualcomm into renegotiating a long-standing contract and royalty arrangement despite the high value Motorola receives from our CDMA patents," Qualcomm Senior Vice President and General Counsel Steve Altman said in a statement.
"Despite Motorola's frequent disparagement of Qualcomm's conduct, Qualcomm and its employees have always acted ethically and responsibly towards Motorola."

On Thursday, Motorola said that although the two companies had signed cross-license agreements in 1990 that grant Qualcomm a royalty-bearing license to use some of Motorola's patents, the patents that are targeted by this latest lawsuit are not licensed to Qualcomm.

Motorola's new complaint contends that Qualcomm's wireless phone products infringe four of Motorola's patents, three of which are the same patents that were the subject of Qualcomm's counter-complaint against Motorola filed in March, Qualcomm said. Motorola filed a patent infringement suit against Qualcomm in March over its wireless Q phone.

"We find it telling that Motorola only now claims that Qualcomm's CDMA phones infringe Motorola's patents," Altman said. "Qualcomm has alleged in the earlier cases that Motorola is attempting to prevent Qualcomm from expanding its share of the wireless phone market at a time when Motorola has no CDMA product offering with which to compete."
